title: AI made expert coders 19% slower
sources: METR (July 2025) randomized controlled trial: 16 experienced open-source developers, 246 tasks in repos they knew; AI-allowed tasks took 19% longer; developers estimated a ~20% speed-up afterwards
Stack Overflow Developer Survey 2025: top frustration (66%) "AI solutions that are almost right, but not quite"
teyro.app: coding track, short daily lessons, real code with instant feedback

lines.text: AI made expert coders *19 percent slower.* | And they thought it made them *faster.*
First, the study. | Researchers at *METR* gave *16* experienced developers | *246* real tasks | in code they already knew well.
Second, with AI tools allowed, | they took *19 percent* longer. | But afterwards, they *believed* AI had sped them up | by about *20 percent.*
Third, why. | A lot of the time went into *reviewing* and *fixing* suggestions | that were *almost* right, | but not quite.
And finally, it's not just them. | In Stack Overflow's developer survey, | *almost right* was the number one frustration | with AI tools.
So AI doesn't replace knowing how to code. | It *rewards* it, | because someone has to spot the *almost.*
If you want to learn to read and fix code properly, | a few minutes a day, | the link's in my *bio.* | It's called *Teyro.*
